subject: Private deployment: next steps & proposed windows for VPC/On‑Prem architecture review
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Walker <tom.walker@hearthhealth.io>
Cc: Sarah Choi <sarah.choi@hearthhealth.io>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — next steps (VPC/on‑prem architecture review)

Hi Tom and Sarah,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion on your compliance constraints and the high‑throughput inference needs for your inference cluster. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Recap: You run inference for the HearthCare product on a hybrid data plane — sensitive PHI data remains in your VPC, and you want Redwood Private to sit in your VPC or on‑prem air‑gapped host.
- Goals for the architecture review: 1) confirm network topology and egress controls, 2) validate latency/throughput SLOs with your target batch sizes, 3) agree on KMS/HSM integration and audit log retention.
- Ask: We should do a 60‑minute technical architecture review with your infra and security owners + our Solutions Eng team. Connor would lead the session from our side.

Proposed 60‑min windows (PST):
- Tue Apr 13, 10:00–11:00
- Wed Apr 14, 13:00–14:00
- Thu Apr 15, 08:30–09:30

If none of those work, share two slots that do and Connor will pick the best fit. Also, if you can share a short network diagram (VPC CIDR, existing VPN/DirectConnect, any strict egress filters) ahead of the meeting that would be super helpful.

Attaching a short precall checklist for the call and our standard private deployment runbook excerpt so we can keep the session focused.

Thanks — looking forward to locking something in.

—
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555‑0124

Attachments: precall-checklist.md (text), private-deploy-runbook-snippet.pdf (text)

Hi Ava — thanks for the clear recap. Wed Apr 14 at 13:00 PST looks good for our infra lead (Sarah) and me. 

A few quick notes before the call:
- We'll want to validate expected outbound endpoints for telemetry (we prefer allowlists rather than broad egress).
- Expect to bring our network engineer and security manager.
- We have a SOC2 questionnaire that I'll attach; we've also surfaced a few questions on KMS key control we want to confirm.

I've attached the SOC2 answers (redacted) and a very rough network sketch. Let us know if you want us to join via our VPN link or use your conference bridge.

Tom
Director, Platform Engineering
Hearth Health

Thanks Tom — wed 2027‑04‑14 13:00 PST is on my calendar. Quick pre‑work so we can be efficient: 

1) Can you confirm the NAT/eBPF or proxy pattern you use for outbound egress? If you prefer allowlist, please include the admin contact so we can coordinate IP ranges.
2) For on‑prem scenarios, do you anticipate an air‑gapped box with manual model packaging, or a secure gateway for docker images? That determines whether we should bring our model packaging engineer.
3) Do you have any tokenization/PII redaction steps in the pipeline we should be aware of (helps with caching/rebatching recommendations).

If it's helpful I can run a 15‑minute network checklist with your infra person 30 minutes before the architecture review. Would that help?

—Connor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai
From: Tom Walker <tom.walker@hearthhealth.io>

Cc: Sarah Choi <sarah.choi@hearthhealth.io>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — next steps (VPC/on‑prem architecture review)

Connor — yes, please run the 15‑minute network checklist at 12:30 PST on Apr 14 (30 min before the main call).

Answers inline: 
- Egress: we run a proxy appliance and prefer allowlists. Admin contact is nets@hearthhealth.io.
- On‑prem: initial plan is a secure gateway that can pull signed images from our internal registry (not fully air‑gapped).
- PII redaction: we do redaction at the ingestion layer (tokenization), so outputs are de‑identified downstream.

I attached the SOC2 answers (full PDF) — please treat as confidential.

Tom
